newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes at fresh low, but $380 holds.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes at fresh low, but $380 holds.

text.p: Gold bullion prices held above the key $380.00 per ounce level on Friday but new buyers were waiting for them to go lower before making a move on the market, dealers said.
Gold was fixed at $380.30 per ounce after $380.45 on Thursday, to set a fresh low since September 6 last year.
"There was been no sign of real buying so far today at $380.00. In fact, if anything gold is looking a little top heavy," one dealer said.
Others claimed that Middle East origin buying had come into the market already to prop prices around fixing level.
"There was a little of that Thursday," another dealer said, adding that some silver had also been bought.
Gold's price fall began on Thursday after investment funds disillusioned by the market's lack of progress compared with booming stock and bond markets, began to sell.

The price fall continued on an announcement from International Monetary Fund (IMF) managing director Michel Camdessus that the IMF had the needed majority to sell five million ounces from its reserves to help the poorest nations.
"It (the gold sale) is in the price already," a dealer said.
But another warned that as long as the IMF issue held over the market, gold's chances of rising were severely limited.
The market held around $380.00 despite some dealers forecasting that gold would have to fall to $378.00 or even lower before bouncing.
Dealers also had mixed views on the tensions in the Middle East, with some reasoning that buying would be stimulated by the escalating violence between Israelis and Palestinians.
However, another dealer commented, "Tensions have been around in various places for some time but, unfortunately for the markets, gold has not been influenced at all."
Silver lost about three cents to $4.86. Dealers expected it to slip to around $4.83 before attracting substantial fresh interest.
"It's oversold and could turn around more quickly than the others when the market changes," one dealer said.
There was less optimism on platinum's medium term outlook.
It fixed at a fresh low since January 31, 1994 at $383.75, down $1.50 from the previous low on Thursday. "Investors won't touch it," a dealer said.
